newsitem.title: SPAIN: Trading boosts Madrid stocks, but seen vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: Trading boosts Madrid stocks, but seen vulnerable.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed higher, but off highs on Monday as some profit-taking began to kick in.
Volume was high, boosted by futures-related trading. Short term the bourse is seen vulnerable with final investment expected to be scant before the budget, due about end-September.
The general index added 1.82 points, 0.51 percent, to 359.82 and the Ibex rose 22.32 points, 0.55 percent, to 4,101.63.

Repsol rose 10 pesetas to 4,250, off a high after a huge put-through this morning. The stock is being helped by something of a change in sentiment on better prospects for the chemicals industry and its favourable position in a domestic price war.
Viscofan added 85 pesetas to 1,900 after a series of broker visits to the company, dealers said.
Bond market gains also helped today's positive climate, but the rally was seen short-lived, at least until the government unveils the 1997 budget.
"I think we've seen our last good day for a bit. The market doesn't really look healthy," said one trader.
